title: CYBRIK internal service-delegation trust metadata v1
description: The pinned trust configuration a relying party (Cyber AI) uses to validate W2-F delegation tokens, and the descriptor of the SOC downstream-mint authority that issues them (ADR-0006 E2/E3; ADR-0008). It fixes the fail-closed defaults as structural constants: sender-constrained (require_cnf) and mutually-authenticated (require_mtls) are const true; max_token_ttl_seconds is const 120 (a longer-lived delegation token is not a valid W2-F token); accepted_algs are asymmetric-only. Public trust (JWKS) is carried by REFERENCE only; no key material is inline, and no operational endpoint is declared. $id uses the RFC 2606 .example documentation domain. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA). Accepted at Gate W2-F (Codex under Founder delegation, 2026-07-24).

trust_domain.description: The internal trust domain this relying party belongs to. The external-authority (A05) boundary is a distinct trust context and its identities are never accepted here (ADR-0007 OD-3).

self_audience.description: This relying party's own audience identifier. An incoming token whose aud is not exactly this value MUST be rejected (RFC 9700 §2.3 audience restriction; confused-deputy defense).

accepted_issuers.description: The pinned set of SOC mint-authority issuer ids. A token whose iss is not in this set MUST be rejected (RFC 8725 §3.8 issuer pinning); an empty set trusts nothing (fail-closed).

accepted_algs.description: The asymmetric-only algorithm allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1). Every entry is a jwtAlg (no HS*/none is expressible); a token whose header.alg is outside this list MUST be rejected.

max_token_ttl_seconds.description: Hard ceiling on token lifetime (exp - iat). Const 120: a W2-F delegation token is short-lived by construction; the relying party MUST reject a token whose lifetime exceeds this even if its signature verifies.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Permitted clock skew when evaluating nbf/exp. Bounded small; a large skew would defeat the short-TTL guarantee.

require_cnf.description: Const true: a delegation token MUST be certificate-bound (RFC 8705 cnf). A bearer (non-sender-constrained) token is never accepted.

require_mtls.description: Const true: the transport MUST be mutually-authenticated mTLS (E2). The token's cnf is verified against the mTLS peer certificate.

mint_authority.description: OPTIONAL descriptor of the SOC downstream-mint side (the port that mints delegation tokens). Signing material is referenced, never inline (secretRef); a dev/test scheme MUST NOT hold a production signing key.
